title: Game-Theoretic Data Allocation for Expert Specialization and Routing
abstract: arXiv:2611.25167v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Can the allocation used to train experts also predict which expert will perform best on a prompt? Such a connection would make the intended division of labor inspectable before training and allow the allocation itself to guide inference. We introduce InflEns, a mixture of LoRA experts whose training weights and inference routes come from the same location game in a fixed prompt-trait space. Players choose positions to maximize their expected shares of the prompt distribution, without using expert losses. We utilize the game's kernel-general theoretical criterion for when co-located positions become locally unstable to separation. We evaluate InflEns on a corpus assembled from seven safety-related benchmarks, which demonstrates that the highest-share expert has the lowest held-out response negative log-likelihood (NLL) on approximately 90% of prompts across four kernels under a sharpened simplex representation, compared with approximate

translated_title: 面向专家专业化与路由的博弈论数据分配
translated_abstract: 用于训练专家的数据分配方式是否也能预测哪个专家在给定提示上表现最佳？若存在这样的联系，将使预期的劳动分工在训练之前即可被检验，并允许分配本身来指导推理。我们提出InflEns，一种LoRA专家混合模型，其训练权重与推理路由均来自固定提示-特征空间中的同一个位置博弈。参与者通过选择位置来最大化其在提示分布中的预期份额，而无需使用专家损失。我们利用该博弈的核通用理论准则来判断共置位置何时对分离变得局部不稳定。我们在由七个安全相关基准组成的数据集上评估了InflEns，结果表明：在锐化单纯形表示下，跨四个核，份额最高的专家在约90%的提示上具有最低的留出响应负对数似然（NLL），相比之下……
tldr: 该论文提出InflEns方法，用一个位置博弈同时决定LoRA专家混合的训练数据分配与推理路由，使份额最高的专家在约90%的提示上表现最优，从而让分工在训练前即可检验并用分配本身指导推理。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes InflEns, a mixture of LoRA experts where a single location game determines both training data allocation and inference routing, showing that the highest-share expert achieves the lowest held-out NLL on approximately 90% of prompts.
